title: One orange. Five more treatments.
method: Built-in image_gen. AI interpretations of material processes, not physical prints or period artifacts. No separate metered API backend used.

studies.name: Where the brush runs dry
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make a square original editorial illustration for a visual-language study. Shared scene: a middle-aged woman with a broad ordinary face, substantial hands, and short greying hair, in a plain contemporary crewneck sweatshirt, seated at a kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand. A long curling strip of peel, one simple blue bowl and an open square window complete the scene. Neutral absorbed expression, no gaze or smile at the viewer. No knife. No other objects, no picturesque view, no houseplants, no nostalgic costume. Interpret the scene exclusively through the specified medium; the blue bowl may become monochrome when the medium requires it. The image is the flat artwork itself, never a photographed mockup. No text, letters, signatures, numbers or decorative frame. Do not copy any particular artist.
Material grammar: black ink on clean white absorbent paper, using a broad flat brush and the point of that same brush. One loaded sweep establishes the hair, another the hunched back, and an abrupt angular pool the sleeve. Lines swell under pressure, taper as the brush lifts, then split into visible bristle tracks as the ink runs out. Let the last drag of a stroke be almost absent. No grey wash: black mass, hairline, split dry stroke and untouched white are the whole range. Draw the face with an oblique cheek stroke and a blunt nose hook; do not finish both eyes or model the cheeks. The hands are legible by the encounter of two interrupted strokes around the white oval fruit. The peel is a loose black downward flick. Place the seated figure low left, window high right suggested by an open brush angle, bowl at lower right as a single interrupted oval. The white gaps carry the forearms. Preserve the difference between a fast thin flick and a slow pressured stroke; neither decorative uniform wobble nor shaded pencil drawing. Forceful, abrupt and intimate, with large calm white areas. Avoid all-over texture, ink splashes, ornamental calligraphy, misty landscape, sentimental watercolour and any artificial paper aging.

studies.name: White cut into black
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make a square original editorial illustration for a visual-language study. Shared scene: a middle-aged woman with a broad ordinary face, substantial hands, and short greying hair, in a plain contemporary crewneck sweatshirt, seated at a kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand. A long curling strip of peel, one simple blue bowl and an open square window complete the scene. Neutral absorbed expression, no gaze or smile at the viewer. No knife. No other objects, no picturesque view, no houseplants, no nostalgic costume. Interpret the scene exclusively through the specified medium; the blue bowl may become monochrome when the medium requires it. The image is the flat artwork itself, never a photographed mockup. No text, letters, signatures, numbers or decorative frame. Do not copy any particular artist.
Material grammar: a white-line engraving cut with a burin into dense end-grain boxwood and printed as one black relief impression on clean white paper. Build from BLACK. Each lit surface is carved out with fine white furrows. Tightly grouped curved white cuts follow the cheek, thumb and sleeve fold; wider spacing leaves the dark shirt nearly solid. Tiny wedge-shaped cuts distinguish the orange pith and rough rind. The peel is an unbroken white ribbon curling against a deep black tabletop, so the ordinary action has the power of an emblem. Very fine incisions, disciplined and rhythmic but not a mathematically uniform screen or crosshatch filter. White marks end decisively with the shape of the burin; no soft gray shading. Compact close composition, the woman left of centre, hands large at centre, bowl a dark ellipse edged with fine white cuts at lower right. The window is a hard white rectangular interruption above the hands, with no outside scenery. Let large dark areas remain truly uncut. Graver marks do the descriptive work, not a photorealistic picture with grain on top. No black outlines on a white sketch, no linocut-style broad gouges, no visible woodgrain texture across the image, no antique border, no sepia, no ornamental foliage.

studies.name: An instruction for a small act
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make a square original editorial illustration for a visual-language study. Shared scene: a middle-aged woman with a broad ordinary face, substantial hands, and short greying hair, in a plain contemporary crewneck sweatshirt, seated at a kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand. A long curling strip of peel, one simple blue bowl and an open square window complete the scene. Neutral absorbed expression, no gaze or smile at the viewer. No knife. No other objects, no picturesque view, no houseplants, no nostalgic costume. Interpret the scene exclusively through the specified medium; the blue bowl may become monochrome when the medium requires it. The image is the flat artwork itself, never a photographed mockup. No text, letters, signatures, numbers or decorative frame. Do not copy any particular artist.
Material grammar: an original technical-pen drawing on spotless white drafting paper. Use the same very fine mechanical black line weight throughout. Show the woman, small table, chair, bowl and lone window in a slightly strange shallow oblique drawing: verticals remain vertical, depth edges share a clear parallel direction, with no vanishing-point drama. This is a human action observed with the exactness usually reserved for a machine part. Every cloth fold is a spare straight or carefully swept line, never a loose sketch. The face is a blunt profile with a single small eye mark; avoid a fully rendered portrait. Keep all surfaces white. Permit a tiny local area of perfectly separated short parallel lines at the bent elbow; no all-over hatching, stipple, grey tone or cast shadow. Only the fruit and curling peel receive flat safety orange. Let the repeated straight table edges and square window be interrupted by the one unpredictable peel curve. Place the main action in the lower right half with generous blank space above left. The result should be dry, precise, faintly odd and quietly humane, not a cute infographic or an IKEA instruction sheet. No labels, arrows, measurements, grids, icons, outlines of hidden body anatomy, graphic-design embellishment, paper texture, brushwork, variable line pressure or glossy vector shading.

studies.name: A copy of a copy
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make a square original editorial illustration for a visual-language study. Shared scene: a middle-aged woman with a broad ordinary face, substantial hands, and short greying hair, in a plain contemporary crewneck sweatshirt, seated at a kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand. A long curling strip of peel, one simple blue bowl and an open square window complete the scene. Neutral absorbed expression, no gaze or smile at the viewer. No knife. No other objects, no picturesque view, no houseplants, no nostalgic costume. Interpret the scene exclusively through the specified medium; the blue bowl may become monochrome when the medium requires it. The image is the flat artwork itself, never a photographed mockup. No text, letters, signatures, numbers or decorative frame. Do not copy any particular artist.
Material grammar: a black-and-white xerographic collage whose visual decisions arise from successive photocopying. The woman and hands begin as an ordinary unposed documentary photograph, then repeated high-contrast copying collapses middle tones into clotted velvety toner blacks and stark white gaps. It must look like copy art, not like a digital ink drawing. The cropped face occupies upper left, partly swallowed by a flat black mass; the working hands and orange peel are enormous near the centre. Make the peel a white ribbon lost in places against paper white and regained against the black table. Construct the window from a separate hard-edged rectangular photocopy fragment placed slightly skew to the figure; do not fill it with a view. A rough horizontal pasted-paper seam interrupts only the tabletop. One portion of the peel is laterally stretched by deliberate movement during a copier scan, while the hands remain readable. Grain clusters at transitions of tone, not evenly over the page. Leave the right third mostly plain white, with the bowl's dark rim touching it. No added colour. Flat reproduction of the completed collage with paper joins visible as graphic discontinuities, not cast shadows. Urgent, domestic, unglamorous, with the directness of an artists' inexpensive multiple. No typography, safety pins, punk decorations, ransom-note lettering, generic grunge overlay, distressed border, scratches everywhere, dramatic photographic lighting, smooth grayscale, screen-print dot pattern or photorealistic color.

studies.name: The template and the hand
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make a square original editorial illustration for a visual-language study. Shared scene: a middle-aged woman with a broad ordinary face, substantial hands, and short greying hair, in a plain contemporary crewneck sweatshirt, seated at a kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand. A long curling strip of peel, one simple blue bowl and an open square window complete the scene. Neutral absorbed expression, no gaze or smile at the viewer. No knife. No other objects, no picturesque view, no houseplants, no nostalgic costume. Interpret the scene exclusively through the specified medium; the blue bowl may become monochrome when the medium requires it. The image is the flat artwork itself, never a photographed mockup. No text, letters, signatures, numbers or decorative frame. Do not copy any particular artist.
Invent a specific hybrid visual grammar: reusable industrial STENCILS make the big shapes; a sharp RED COLOUR PENCIL supplies the small human observations. Stencil the sweatshirt and table as broad opaque near-black petrol-green shapes on clean bright white. Their closed forms contain conspicuous clean white support bridges: narrow unpainted rectangular interruptions that hold the interior stencil islands in place. The rigid cut shapes should be blunt and useful rather than elegantly organic. Then use a dry red pencil with a fine uneven waxy deposit to draw only a cheek, one ear, the meeting hands and the curling peel. Keep these red lines slightly displaced from the stencil edge: they have their own job, rather than tracing every silhouette. The orange itself is one flat burnt-orange stencil circle, interrupted by the white shape of a thumb. The bowl is a simple open petrol-green U, and the window two disconnected right-angle stencil shapes. Crop the figure and table strongly toward the lower right so the upper left remains blank. The image's tension comes from a rigid reusable template meeting a fragile specific observation. No modelling, shadows, perspective rendering, face shading, fully outlined limbs or decorative pattern. Avoid distressed military lettering, spray-paint aerosol clouds, paint drips, trendy print misregistration, halftone grain, fashionable retro palette and added kitchen props.
studies.editPrompt: Edit the supplied industrial-stencil and red-pencil illustration. Preserve its current square framing, woman at lower right, dark petrol-green stencil sweatshirt and table, white stencil support-bridge interruptions, large empty white upper-left field, window fragment, bowl, hands and orange-peeling action. Make one focused simplification to the head. REMOVE all grey shading, grey hair rendering, cheek shading, fine facial modelling and little internal hair strands. Replace the hair with a single dark petrol-green stencil shape, interrupted by just two narrow white support bridges and one broad white gap for greying hair. Describe the face with only the thin broken red outline of forehead-nose-chin, one short downward eyelid stroke, one ear loop and one tiny mouth stroke. The entire interior of the face remains pure white. No red blush or hatch, no eyebrows or nostril shading. Keep the face clearly human, middle-aged, absorbed, with its existing profile and pose. Preserve the interesting red-pencil texture around the working hands but remove unnecessary fingernail marks. Do not add any objects or alter the rest of the composition. This is an edit target, not just a style reference.
